Lakers Nation > Blog > Lakers News > Lakers Injury Report: Luka Doncic & Ziaire Williams Out Vs. Clippers Lakers News Lakers Injury Report: Luka Doncic & Ziaire Williams Out Vs. Clippers
 Corey Hansford Published: 10/28/2026 4 Min Read Oct 27, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) reacts against the Portland Trail Blazers in the first half at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images SHARE Luka Doncic (back tightness) and Ziaire Williams (left foot soreness) are listed as out for the Los Angeles Lakers contest against the L.A. Clippers on Wednesday night. Rookie Cameron Carr (right oblique strain) and second-year wing Adou Thiero (left knee injury management) remain out.
 This is the Lakers’ first back-to-back of the season and it will now see them without their leader and the NBA’s leading scorer. Doncic is averaging 36 points per game through the first four games of the season and has scored 41 and 52 points in each of the last two contests. Back tightness is a pretty minor issue overall, so the Lakers are likely just playing it safe for their superstar.
 But that will put Austin Reaves in the spotlight as it will be up to him to step up and lead the Lakers’ offense. This isn’t something he isn’t used to as he had some outstanding performances last season in this same situation, and the Lakers will need more of the same.
 Missing Williams is an unfortunate blow and is likely the Lakers playing things safe once again as he did miss time in the preseason with a contusion to that same foot. Williams’ presence will be missed on both ends of the court as he has been the Lakers’ primary point-of-attack defender, but is also averaging 11.3 points per game and knocking down 46.7% from 3-point range.
 With Carr and Thiero still not ready to make their season debuts, the Lakers’ depth will be tested and head coach JJ Redick will have to rely on some players who haven’t had an opportunity so far this season. Quentin Grimes and Jake LaRavia would be the most likely candidates to step into the starting lineup, which would leave Collin Sexton and Sandro Mamukelashvili as the two normal rotation players coming off the bench.
 Jaden Hardy or Bronny James would seem likely to get a shot, as could veteran wing Jarred Vanderbilt if Redick feels the Lakers could use a bit of attitude and defensive energy off the bench. Center Kevon Looney could also see a potential increase in playing time, though he has struggled in his limited minutes so far this season.
 Lakers’ rookie Cameron Carr goes through first full practice
 There was some positive news on the injury front as Redick revealed that Carr did go through his first full practice of the season with the Coachella Valley Lakers and should be back soon.
 “We’re still working through that. He was able to get a full practice today,” Redick said. “With five games in seven nights, we’re not gonna be able to practice this week and wanted to be cognizant of his ramp-up and what he needed to do to be back in our lineup. Today was a good step for him.”
 As for exactly what needs to be done for Carr to make his NBA debut, Redick noted that getting through a full practice was the biggest step.
 “We needed him to be able to get through a full practice, so that’s probably a very important step,” Redick added. “Obviously he was able to do some level of conditioning because it was an upper body injury. But want to make sure he’s able to take hits and able to be in shape.”
